pillar_reactions.evidence: He tied it forward to his own goals rather than just agreeing, and asked ahead about progression: 'I was just thinking about like, what weight am I at in the end of six months? What am I pushing with the double snatches and, you know, just going up a kilo.' He also volunteered the graduate-in-six-months principle back to the rep in his own words — 'I'd rather you guys teach me how to fish than just give me the fish' — and closed the segment with 'Yeah, that's awesome.' The pillar also answered a problem he had already diagnosed himself, that body-part splits plus separate zone-two cardio would need three hours he does not have.

No resistance and no questions — 'any questions on nutrition' / 'no, I'm excited to get this journey started.' He had already conceded nutrition as his weakest link ('for sure nutrition, but that's on me'). The travel-specific application, what to pick on a menu on the road, was the part aimed at his actual failure mode, and he accepted it without probing how it would work across the one week in four he is away.

The strongest reaction of the three. On the rep saying Trevor will chase a missed workout, he answered 'That's a good one. Yeah, I need that', and then volunteered his own failure analysis unprompted: 'if I miss a workout, it's not because I woke up and I had a motivation. It's usually like something out of my control... I traveled for work or my wife, we went. It's, I got to change my whole schedule up.' That is a prospect handing the rep the precise mechanism the pillar needs to solve, and it went unreflected.

anchors.raw: I do, just because we bought a house, so I spent literally $300,000 on my own cash for a down payment. So anyways, I don't have any cash, but I just picked up a second job
anchors.note: The dominant financial fact of the call. A $300,000 cash deposit consumed his liquidity entirely, and the mortgage is now absorbing half of a second job's income. Unlike the Felipe Dublanc renovation four days earlier, this constraint has no end date — it is a permanent step down in disposable income, not a temporary squeeze.

anchors.raw: Because I had a couple of collections that were, like I was fighting a couple of collections last year. I spent the last year doing credit repairs. I think I'm back in the 700s, like literally this morning, but like 7.06.
anchors.note: He checked his own FICO that morning and had only just recovered into the 700s after a year of repair work and contested collections. The score was then used as the qualifying asset for a twelve-month credit application taken out minutes later. Records as an anchor because it is the clearest available signal of what this buyer could actually absorb, and it pointed the opposite way from the decision taken.

anchors.raw: I just picked up a second job, so I definitely have an extra, you know, that side job. It gives me roughly around, but yeah, about 2,400 extra, which half of it I need to use towards my mortgage, but I definitely can set aside $1,000 every month.
anchors.note: The only genuine affordability signal, and it is a monthly one rather than a liquid one. He priced himself at $1,000 a month before the rep quoted anything, which is why the $1,200 route was accepted with only a mild remark and the $662 twelve-month route felt comfortable. It also means the entire purchase is serviced from a second job.

anchors.raw: I've been watching Trevor for maybe a year, like it's been a whole year that I've been watching... Trevor's the only one that you can't practice what you preach, and so it's hard to listen to a guy about nutrition if he's not following nutrition, so at least Trevor's actually practicing what he's coaching
anchors.note: Twelve months of free content consumption before booking, and he arrived having already disqualified the competition on authenticity grounds. He even tracked visible physique changes in Trevor over that period as evidence the method works. This is the strongest pre-sold position in the batch and it is why no fear, doubt or think-about-it objection ever surfaced.

anchors.raw: all my sisters and my parents, everyone doesn't like fitness, and so you can see that it's really hitting them really hard, right, all of them that take medication, high blood pressure, know, type 2 diabetes
anchors.note: The cost of inaction is visible to him daily in his own family, and he volunteered it. This is the raw material for a consequence frame and the rep used it for a role-model frame instead. Recorded as a supporting anchor because it is the number-free version of what makes $6,000 look cheap to this buyer.

anchors.raw: is there any way I can make monthly payments on that plan, like every month, I complete, it's like another $1,000.
anchors.note: He converted $6,000 into $1,000 a month himself and treated it as workable before any structure was offered. His only price reaction all call was noticing the instalment uplift — 'so we're adding an extra 200?' — and accepting it immediately.

unmet_demand.want: Measurable VO2 max improvement, which he researched independently and named as a priority
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He raised it twice and made it central to his reasoning — 'the studies show that VO2 max has an impact on the quality of life' — and asked where he could get tested. The rep agreed it correlates with longevity and then folded it into the general kettlebell conditioning claim without addressing measurement, testing, protocol or whether the programme targets it at all. He had already half-answered it himself by speculating that short-rest circuits might deliver a zone-two effect. Whether the programme improves or tracks VO2 max is genuinely unestablished.

unmet_demand.want: Training and nutrition that survive one week in every three or four on the road
unmet_demand.why_unmet: This is his single biggest structural problem and he named it as the source of his inconsistency. The programme does appear to answer it — portability, hotel gyms, adjustable weeks, advance notice to the coach — and the rep covered all of that. Recording it because the nutrition half was answered only in principle ('what to pick in the menu') with nothing concrete for a man who currently defaults to Chipotle bowls and Chick-fil-A nuggets for a full week at a time.

unmet_demand.want: Rehabilitation of an untreated knee producing instability and muscular imbalance under single-leg load
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep promised bespoke mobility protocols for the tight hips and core, which addresses the downstream symptom rather than the untreated joint. Nobody asked whether a clinician had ever seen it, and the one professional group that would assess it was undermined in the same breath. Whether a remote kettlebell programme can safely load and progress this knee toward double snatches is unestablished and no qualified person was involved in the question.

unmet_demand.want: To know what the twelve-month financed plan costs in total
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Never stated. He read '$662' off his own screen and asked what it meant; the answer he received explained who he pays, not what he pays. Over twelve months that implies roughly $7,944 against a $6,000 headline, and neither figure nor difference was spoken by the rep.
